beginner.summary: For developers and data or platform engineers who can write Python and have called an LLM API at least once, and who want to design systems in which several LLM agents cooperate. Covers when a single agent is enough and when to split, agent roles and contracts, message passing, sequential pipelines, supervisor routing, parallel fan-out, shared state and the blackboard idea, memory scopes, handoffs, critic and debate patterns, per-agent tool permissions, stop conditions and budgets, trace reading, first failure modes, human checkpoints and a research-team capstone. Examples stay framework-neutral and are compared with LangGraph, AutoGen and CrewAI.
prerequisites: Writes Python 3 programs with functions, classes, dataclasses and virtual environments
Has called a chat-completion style LLM API and read the JSON response, including the usage token counts
Has a laptop with Python 3.11 or later, git, a terminal and either a hosted model API key or a local model server such as Ollama
outcomes: Decide with evidence whether a task needs one agent or several, using a measured single-agent baseline
Build supervisor, pipeline, fan-out and critic designs from plain Python and map them to LangGraph, AutoGen and CrewAI concepts
Define agent roles, message formats, shared state, memory scopes and tool permissions as explicit contracts
Run, trace and bound a small agent team with turn limits, budgets and a human approval step
